title: hello-procode — a pro-grade terminal coding companion (target: cli)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “A full coding agent — exploration, edits, tests, a fleet of sub-agents — from one YAML.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beats.

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec, block by block

beats.label: The header: what it is, what to ask it
beats.cue: The header is the pitch — explore, edit, test, fan out a fleet, loop until it's done.

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: Two lines: what it's called, and which runtime spine to compile.

beats.label: Model, depth, failover
beats.cue: Opus, a 16384-token per-turn budget (the runtime default is 8192), and a fallback chain.

beats.label: Three operating postures
beats.cue: STANDARD, ULTRACODE, GOAL — sticky for the session, and the user sets them, not the model.

beats.label: The Method, every turn
beats.cue: UNDERSTAND → PLAN → EXECUTE → VERIFY. “Never edit a file you have not read.”

beats.label: Workflows: the fan-out rule
beats.cue: One batched turn. Read-only workers run concurrently; anything that executes or writes serializes.

beats.label: Goal mode
beats.cue: “/loop” writes the completion condition to GOAL.md — on disk, so the goal outlives the context.

beats.label: Work that runs long
beats.cue: Bash defaults to 30 seconds; background processes, --continue to resume, --prompt for one shot.

beats.label: Durable memory, and the rules
beats.cue: Remember what the code doesn't say. Never force-push, reset --hard, rm -rf, or sudo.

beats.label: The first two workers
beats.cue: A read-only codebase mapper, and a test runner allow-listed to test commands only.

beats.label: The orchestrator
beats.cue: The only worker holding Task: decompose, fan out, cross-check, synthesize — it never edits.

beats.label: reviewer + security-auditor
beats.cue: Read-only, on Haiku, and the only shell they get is read-only git — `git diff` and `git show` for both, plus `git log` for the reviewer.

beats.label: debugger + docs-writer
beats.cue: The debugger names a root cause and does NOT fix; the docs-writer may write Markdown, nothing else.

beats.label: The independent verifier
beats.cue: “You did NOT do the work — judge it cold.” The worker never grades its own paper.

beats.label: Sixteen tools
beats.cue: Files and shell, background-process polling, and AST blast-radius analysis before a refactor.

beats.label: Memory and the feedback loop
beats.cue: memory: remembers across sessions; feedback: turns your thumbs-up into a training dataset.

beats.label: The hard denials, first
beats.cue: Six patterns denied outright — and written at the TOP. Within a layer the FIRST matching rule wins, so a deny below the catch-all alwaysAsk would never fire.

beats.label: The always-on grants
beats.cue: Reads, edits, web, todos, codegraph, memory — friction-free, because coding needs them.

beats.label: Fence the shell
beats.cue: A named allow-list for the everyday commands, then one alwaysAsk that catches every other Bash.

beats.label: Compact on a cheap model
beats.cue: At 85% of the context window the runtime snips and summarizes — on Haiku, not on Opus.

beats.label: The cold-start banner
beats.cue: Four rotating taglines, printed once when the *compiled bundle* boots — codegen-only, so `crewhaus run` never shows them. “Fan out. Cross-check. Verify. Done.”

beats.label: The commented-out extras
beats.cue: Left off on purpose: a hard spend cap, the two-tier turn router, and an MCP server.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the scope audit — nothing emitted yet.

beats.label: Audit its own tool grants
beats.cue: Keyword-matches the builtins against the instructions: implied-but-missing on top, possible over-grants below. Read the top line as a prompt, not a verdict — `imageGenerate` matched the rule that tells this agent to REFUSE image generation.

verify.note: keyword matcher over agent.instructions — reports 17 of the 22 builtins (1 implied-but-missing, 10 present, 6 possible over-grants); the imageGenerate hit is a known false positive off crewhaus.yaml's refusal rule

beats.label: Lower the spec to IR
beats.cue: The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees. Straight to a file — no pager, so the exit code is the compiler's.

verify.note: writes the lowered IR to live/ir.json; the next beat opens it

beats.label: Open the lowered IR
beats.cue: The instructions land as one inlined string; scroll to the bottom for the lowered blocks — compaction, feedback, memory, continuity, banner.

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: --check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN with no key.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the credentials gate

beats.label: Open the emitted agent
beats.cue: The whole fleet and every permission rule, compiled into one TypeScript program you own.

beats.label: Launch the coding REPL
beats.cue: [needs-key] Compiles in memory and opens in whatever directory you're standing in — here, the starter's own harness.

verify.note: interactive REPL; needs Anthropic credentials. Its workspace is the demo terminal's cwd (this starter), so the prompts below are scoped to files that live here.

beats.label: Ask it to map the harness
beats.cue: [needs-key] It dispatches code-explorer in its own context instead of grepping turn after turn.
beats.text: map .crewhaus/ and crewhaus.yaml — what slash commands, skills and sub-agents does this harness ship? 5 bullets

verify.note: scoped to .crewhaus/ + crewhaus.yaml deliberately: the tool workspace is the terminal's cwd, and by this point live/dist/node_modules has put ~13k vendored files under it — an unscoped "explore this repo" reads them

beats.label: Flip to ULTRACODE and audit
beats.cue: [needs-key] Exhaustive mode — security-auditor and reviewer fan out in one batched turn.
beats.text: /ultracode then audit this harness's own permission rules — the permissions block in crewhaus.yaml and .crewhaus/settings.json — for anything a coding agent could talk its way past

verify.note: both named files exist in this starter

beats.label: Run a one-off workflow
beats.cue: [needs-key] Decompose, dispatch the fleet, cross-check the returns, synthesize one ranked report.
beats.text: /workflow cross-check .crewhaus/ against crewhaus.yaml — which commands, skills and sub-agents does the spec never mention, and which does it mention with no file on disk?

verify.note: a real answer lives here: .crewhaus/sub-agents/perf-reviewer.md is a worker the spec never names — the 'One more thing' beat opens it

beats.label: Exit — and rate the session
beats.cue: [needs-key] The feedback: block turns the exit into a one-keystroke [g]ood/[b]ad rating.

beats.label: Reopen the same conversation
beats.cue: [needs-key] --continue resumes the most recent session for this spec; autoRecall reloads memories.

verify.note: resumes the session the previous beats created; needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Exit
beats.cue: [needs-key] Back to the shell.

beats.label: Boot the compiled bundle instead
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same fleet, no CLI in the loop — and this is the one place the banner you typed actually prints.

verify.note: cli.banner is codegen-only — the emitted bundle prints it at boot; `crewhaus run` never does. Deps were installed by prove-check's --check.

beats.label: Exit
beats.cue: [needs-key] Back to the shell.

groups.title: One more thing · nothing here needed a recompile

beats.label: A slash command is a Markdown file
beats.cue: Ten of them ship in .crewhaus/commands/ — drop in your own and it appears at startup.

beats.label: A fleet worker the spec never mentions
beats.cue: Resolved from .crewhaus/sub-agents/ at Task time — read-only, so it's parallel-eligible.

beats.label: The hook behind the rules
beats.cue: A pre-tool hook in its own process, backstopping the deny rules the model can't talk its way past.

beats.label: Export the fleet as a Claude Code plugin
beats.cue: The same spec, emitted as a plugin dir — one agent file per sub-agent, plus a skill.

beats.label: Open the exported orchestrator
beats.cue: Your orchestrator, now a Claude Code sub-agent. One spec, more than one runtime.
